clue.text: Send off little man to trading area

parts.note: Des is a short form of the man's name Desmond, so a 'little' version of a man's name
a patch is a salesperson's or trader's territory

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatching a junior employee to a market district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little man' is not a small person but a shortened man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch or post something is to send it on its way.

clue.text: Daughter Jane, a striking person

parts.note: Jane Asher is a well-known British actress

explanation.surface: A girl called Jane is described as a remarkable figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Asher is a British actress and cake-maker, famous in the 1960s; the surname is what the clue wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A dasher is an old word for a dashing, stylish person who cuts a fine figure.

clue.text: Thus I was first to get dirty

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
to have led is to have been first, at the front

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being the first to get muddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soiled has been stained or made unclean.

clue.text: By chance, drink to a Conservative

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone happens to buy a pint for a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory describes something depending on luck or random outcome.

clue.text: College poem put in cipher

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A university verse is encrypted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a secret system of writing, which is a code.

clue.text: One zone gone over by fat reptile

indicators.note: the fat is laid over and around the other letters, covering them inside it

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single area has been covered by a greasy lizard-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over by' puts IZ inside LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard is a scaly four-legged reptile.

clue.text: Small and cosy home taken by the enemy

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
'time, the enemy' is a familiar phrase, time being the foe that ages us

explanation.surface: A snug little house is seized by hostile forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a well-worn saying, so 'the enemy' can stand for TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Intime is a French borrowing describing an intimate, cosy setting.

clue.text: Good in terms of order synonymous with traditional values

explanation.surface: A description of something neat that also embodies old-fashioned virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order means perfectly neat, and the dessert is an American symbol of wholesome traditional values.

clue.text: Laughing stock in side or out?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A teasing question about whether a figure of fun is on the team or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of IN SIDE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is mockery, and a laughing stock is an object of it, so the two stand loosely for each other.

clue.text: After second hint stops making payments

indicators.note: the hint is placed after the letter for second in the answer

parts.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
ends means stops

explanation.surface: After a moment's suggestion, someone stops paying money.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular sums of money such as salaries or allowances.

clue.text: Lethargy of good person up against soldiers

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
taken as written
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is sluggish when facing an army.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) for soldiers and ST (saint) for a good person are crossword conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, sluggish state of near-unconsciousness.

clue.text: Operatic work in event entertaining our queen

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a thing can be an event or occasion
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An opera is staged at a function attended by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like a hint about a show, but it is the containment signal; the opera meant is Wagner's four-part cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle is a famous set of four operas.

clue.text: Things that happen in flat, things in extremis

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: in extremis literally means at the extremes, so the word's first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A description of household goods in an apartment at a crisis point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' takes the first and last letters of 'things', T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are occurrences, happenings.

clue.text: Rooms in which honoured person is entertained by cleaners

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: chars are charwomen, British domestic cleaners
an MBE is a Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honours award

explanation.surface: A decorated guest is welcomed by the domestic staff in certain rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour; char is British slang for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are rooms, especially private or official ones.

clue.text: Mediocre state coming with mature years

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
age means advanced years

explanation.surface: A remark that one becomes ordinary as one grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means middling, ordinary, nothing special.

clue.text: Daring item of underwear? Extremely!

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
very means extremely

explanation.surface: A racy piece of lingerie is described as highly bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery is courage, the quality of being bold.

clue.text: Car two miles back not completely visible

indicators.note: back tells us the letters run in reverse order
only part of the words can be seen, so a run of letters is buried inside them

explanation.surface: A vehicle a couple of miles away is partly out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely visible' finds OMIL inside 'two miles'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is a large luxurious car.

clue.text: Earnest professional joining institute

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to institute something is to found it

explanation.surface: A serious expert joins an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means deep and serious in feeling, close to earnest.

clue.text: Nice plan put out for architectural feature

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A pleasant design is presented for a building's detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a small pointed turret on a roof or buttress.

clue.text: Requirement for long hair principal prohibited, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer sounds like the phrase rather than being spelt that way

parts.note: a head is a principal, and banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: A school head forbids long hair, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A headband is a strip worn round the head to keep long locks in place.

clue.text: Banter from returning storyteller

indicators.note: returning means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untruths

explanation.surface: Teasing chat from a narrator coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to jeer or rant, an old sense close to taunting banter.

clue.text: Son going after country girl

indicators.note: going after means placed behind the other piece in the answer

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A boy pursues a young woman from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances is a woman's first name.

clue.text: It's easy finding account in collection of papers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a file is a collection of papers

explanation.surface: Finding a record in a folder is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means effortless, achieved without difficulty.

clue.text: Girl with rubbish piled up has bill to settle

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society girl

indicators.note: in a down clue piled up means the word is stacked bottom to top, reading backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A young woman with a heap of garbage still owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' turns ROT into TOR, read upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor is a person who owes money and must pay.

clue.text: Plant beginning to die — is mistake admitted?

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a plant starting to wilt was their error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'die', and 'admitted' signals letting the mistake into the short word; the dash makes it read as a question about a wilting plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Derris is a tropical climbing plant whose roots yield an insecticide.

clue.text: A dance enthusiast, man with energy

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
Dan is a man's name
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A keen and lively man takes to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance for couples.

clue.text: Remain faithful in this place following active duty

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first in the answer

parts.note: AD is an abbreviation for active duty
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A soldier stays loyal at this post after active service.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick to a cause or belief.

clue.text: Once again fix rising river

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: Repairs again a river that is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it a second time.

clue.text: Old city church involved with mischievous kid

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
to be in something is to be involved; the answer's letters also run across 'church involved', a coincidence since 'Old city' then has no job

explanation.surface: An ancient church gets mixed up with a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, impish youngster.

clue.text: Bottle and tin in hamper

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to hamper is to deter or impede
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A bottle and a tin packed into a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a basket but is a verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass bottle for serving wine.

clue.text: Less shallow river — someone has pulled son out

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: pulled and out together tell us letters are taken away from the word
out, with pulled, signals the removal of letters

parts.note: a person is someone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river that's not shallow, from which someone has rescued a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled ... out' removes SON from PERSON, leaving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeper is the comparative of deep, the opposite of shallow.

clue.text: Us hard on wayward republic

indicators.note: wayward means straying, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone is being tough on unruly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a Central American republic.
